sentences.en: And it is explicitly clear in the South, race is the strongest predictor of political leanings, more than any other, more than gender, more than age, more than religious
sentences.zh: 在南方，这一点非常明确，种族是政治倾向最强的预测指标，超过任何其他因素，超过性别，超过年龄，超过宗教

sentences.en: beliefs, race.
sentences.zh: 信仰，种族。

sentences.en: Central to this is the shift in population, the demographic changes.
sentences.zh: 这其中的核心是人口的转移，即人口结构的变化。

sentences.en: Walk us through that.
sentences.zh: 带我们了解一下。

sentences.en: What was happening in Georgia?
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州发生了什么？

sentences.en: Between 2000 and 2010, Georgia was very solidly a Republican state.
sentences.zh: 在2000年到2010年之间，佐治亚州非常稳固地是一个共和党州。

sentences.en: But at the exact same time, there was this massive influx of African Americans as part of a reverse migration.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，作为反向移民的一部分，大量非裔美国人涌入。

sentences.en: There was a dramatic increase of, I think, 96% in the Latino population in the state.
sentences.zh: 该州的拉丁裔人口出现了惊人的增长，我想是96%。

sentences.en: And there was a fast rising Asian American Pacific Islander population.
sentences.zh: 亚裔美国人和太平洋岛民人口也在迅速增长。

sentences.en: And all of those populations were ripe for outreach.
sentences.zh: 所有这些群体都已成熟，可以进行外联。

sentences.en: African Americans were the most likely to be Democratic-leaning voters.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人是最有可能倾向于民主党的选民。

sentences.en: And when Abrams looked at the numbers, she realized that Democrats were losing statewide elections by around 200,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 当艾布拉姆斯查看这些数据时，她意识到民主党在全州选举中输掉了大约20万张选票。

sentences.en: But...
sentences.zh: 但是……

sentences.en: We had 800,000 unregistered people of color, 600,000 of whom were African American.
sentences.zh: 我们有80万未登记的有色人种，其中60万是非裔美国人。

sentences.en: We had this extraordinary opportunity to reach people who had never been engaged.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个绝佳的机会去接触那些从未参与过政治的人。

sentences.en: They were new.
sentences.zh: 他们是新人。

sentences.en: And we were new.
sentences.zh: 而我们也是新人。

sentences.en: And we had to build instead of, you know, manifesting.
sentences.zh: 我们必须去建设，而不是，你知道，空想。

sentences.en: The strategy Abrams was trying to sell was not intuitive to many longstanding party members.
sentences.zh: 艾布拉姆斯试图推销的策略，对许多老牌党员来说并不直观。

sentences.en: I'm arguing, stop trying to get back the thing that worked for 130 years.
sentences.zh: 我的主张是，别再试图找回那套过去130年行之有效的方法了。

sentences.en: There is an absolute logic to rejecting what I said.
sentences.zh: 拒绝我的说法是有绝对逻辑的。

sentences.en: They still believed it was possible to put back together this coalition of white rule voters
sentences.zh: 他们仍然相信，有可能重新拼凑起那个白人统治选民的联盟，

sentences.en: who, along with Black urban voters, still allowed the party to sporadically win elections.
sentences.zh: 那个联盟曾与黑人城市选民一起，让该党偶尔能赢得选举。

sentences.en: Also not intuitive was the work Abrams believed it would take to win over these currently disengaged voters,
sentences.zh: 同样不直观的，还有艾布拉姆斯认为赢得这些目前不参与政治的选民所需付出的努力，

sentences.en: which was a very grassroots, one-voter-at-a-time approach, as if they were building a community church.
sentences.zh: 那是一种非常草根的、逐个争取选民的方法，就像在建立一个社区教堂一样。

sentences.en: How did you get others on board with this strategy?
sentences.zh: 你是如何让其他人接受这个策略的？

sentences.en: I got on a plane and I started traveling around the country to meet donors who had given to democratic causes who would take a meeting with me.
sentences.zh: 我坐上飞机，开始在全国各地奔波，去见那些曾为民主党事业捐款、并愿意与我见面的人。

sentences.en: And I would walk into these meetings.
sentences.zh: 我会走进这些会议室。

sentences.en: I would show them this PowerPoint presentation.
sentences.zh: 我会向他们展示这份PPT演示文稿。

sentences.en: Some of them would let me get all the way through it.
sentences.zh: 有些人会让我完整地讲完。

sentences.en: A handful of folks said, yes, we will support you.
sentences.zh: 少数人说，是的，我们会支持你。

sentences.en: We will inveSt.
sentences.zh: 我们会投资。

sentences.en: Many, many more said, you're so cute, very, you know, sort of patting me on my head.
sentences.zh: 更多更多的人说，你真可爱，你知道的，就像是在摸我的头一样。

sentences.en: But the goal there was we had to be a full-time party to meet the Republican, you know, juggernaut.
sentences.zh: 但我们的目标是，为了应对共和党的，你知道，那股巨头势力，我们必须成为一个全职政党。

sentences.en: I raised money from labor unions, from individuals, from organizations.
sentences.zh: 我从工会、个人和组织那里筹集资金。

sentences.en: And then I used those dollars to just constantly be in the presence of communities to engage them.
sentences.zh: 然后我用这些钱不断地出现在社区中，去动员他们。

sentences.en: So she took that money she was able to raise and she embedded organizers into communities, sometimes months before elections.
sentences.zh: 于是，她利用筹集到的资金，在选举前几个月甚至更早，就将组织者派驻到了社区中。

sentences.en: One thing I learned from my mom, who had to combine three churches and was growing her church in Mississippi,
sentences.zh: 我从我母亲那里学到的一件事是——她曾在密西西比州合并了三个教堂并壮大了她的教会——

sentences.en: was that she said, you meet people where they are, not where you want them to be.
sentences.zh: 她说，你要去人们所在的地方见他们，而不是去你希望他们所在的地方。

sentences.en: If you want a community to trust you, they need to believe that you understand their pain.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让一个社区信任你，他们需要相信你理解他们的痛苦。

sentences.en: In 2013, I deployed the staff that I built to go across the state and hold listening sessions.
sentences.zh: 2013年，我部署了我建立的团队，走遍全州举行倾听会议。

sentences.en: And we intentionally held them in rural parts of Georgia, where there were very few people of color and possibly no Democrats, but we found a few.
sentences.zh: 我们特意在佐治亚州的农村地区举行会议，那里几乎没有有色人种，可能也没有民主党人，但我们确实找到了一些。

sentences.en: But we went to every region and we talked about, again, education, economics, and shared responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我们去了每一个地区，再次谈论教育、经济和共同责任。

sentences.en: I did a Korean radio show for one session where I got on the radio every Friday and let it get translated into Korean.
sentences.zh: 有一次我做了一个韩语广播节目，我每周五上电台，让它被翻译成韩语。

sentences.en: It was one of the slowest shows in human history because I don't speak Korean.
sentences.zh: 那是人类历史上最慢的节目之一，因为我不会说韩语。

sentences.en: This strategy went on for years.
sentences.zh: 这个策略持续了多年。

sentences.en: Slowly but surely, by the end of 2014, Abrams' nonprofit group, the New Georgia Project, along with other allied groups, had registered more than 100,000 voters.
sentences.zh: 缓慢但坚定地，到2014年底，艾布拉姆斯的非营利组织“新佐治亚项目”以及其他盟友组织，已经登记了超过10万名选民。

sentences.en: Fast forward 16, we picked up a few seats, we did better.
sentences.zh: 快进到16年，我们赢得了一些席位，我们表现得更好。

sentences.en: And then, of course, 2018, where we were able to demonstrate, I think, on every metric, the utility of our project.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有2018年，我认为我们在每一个指标上都证明了我们项目的效用。

sentences.en: We are writing the next chapter of Georgia's future, where no one is unseen, no one is unheard, and no one is uninspired.
sentences.zh: 我们正在书写佐治亚州未来的新篇章，在这里，没有人被忽视，没有人被遗忘，没有人失去希望。

sentences.en: Stacey Abrams, get to know her.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯，去了解一下她。

sentences.en: She's the woman who won the big Democratic gubernatorial primary last night in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 她就是昨晚在佐治亚州赢得民主党州长初选的那位女性。

sentences.en: Stacey Abrams will try to become the first female black governor in U.S.
sentences.zh: 今年秋天，斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯将尝试成为美国历史上第一位黑人女性州长。

sentences.en: history this fall.
sentences.zh: 历史。

sentences.en: She won the Georgia Democrat...
sentences.zh: 她赢得了佐治亚州民主党……

sentences.en: It was in 2018 when Abrams ran for governor.
sentences.zh: 那是2018年，艾布拉姆斯竞选州长的时候。

sentences.en: I'd been building this idea for a party strategy for a decade.
sentences.zh: 十年来，我一直在构思这个政党策略。

sentences.en: And it was in the guise of a gubernatorial election that I could test out every facet of the plan.
sentences.zh: 正是借着州长选举的幌子，我可以测试这个计划的每一个方面。

sentences.en: She says the idea was, I think this strategy might be ready for a real road teSt.
sentences.zh: 她说当时的想法是，我想这个策略可能已经准备好进行真正的实地测试了。

sentences.en: Why not run myself to find out?
sentences.zh: 为什么不亲自参选来验证一下呢？

sentences.en: We lose elections as Democrats by about 200,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 作为民主党人，我们输掉选举通常是因为大约20万张选票的差距。

sentences.en: My mission is to have a clear, resounding message that is bold and ambitious, and that is detailed, and that we take to every single voter.
sentences.zh: 我的使命是传达一个清晰、响亮、大胆且雄心勃勃的信息，并且要详尽，我们要把它带给每一位选民。

sentences.en: I wanted to be the governor.
sentences.zh: 我想成为州长。

sentences.en: I wanted to deliver on these ideas.
sentences.zh: 我想实现这些想法。

sentences.en: But my only credible way of running was to test my theory.
sentences.zh: 但我唯一可信的参选方式就是测试我的理论。

sentences.en: What we are doing differently is that we spent the bulk of our investment not on television, but on the ground,
sentences.zh: 我们所做的不同之处在于，我们将大部分投资没有花在电视上，而是花在基层，

sentences.en: building an army that we believe we can scale and we can take the entire state with by November.
sentences.zh: 建立了一支我们相信可以扩大规模的队伍，并以此在11月拿下整个州。

sentences.en: And that November, when she faced off against her Republican opponent...
sentences.zh: 那年11月，当她面对共和党对手时……

sentences.en: We not only increased our performance among every single one of those communities of color, among young people,
sentences.zh: 我们不仅在每一个有色人种社区、在年轻人中的表现都有所提升，

sentences.en: we increased white participation for Democrats for the first time in nearly 30 years.
sentences.zh: 我们还近30年来首次增加了白人对民主党的参与度。

sentences.en: It was a bit startling.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人吃惊。

sentences.en: I'm like, oh, hey, it does work.
sentences.zh: 我心想，噢，嘿，它确实有效。

sentences.en: Everyone, you know, if these values are real and if they are credible, you will attract people to you and they will support the work you need to do.
sentences.zh: 每个人，你知道，如果这些价值观是真实的且可信的，你就会吸引人们来到你身边，他们会支持你需要做的工作。

sentences.en: But because of the aggressive use of voter suppression and other challenges,
sentences.zh: 但由于选民压制和其他挑战的激进使用，

sentences.en: I did not become governor and therefore I publicly didn't get a job I really, really wanted and worked really hard to get.
sentences.zh: 我没能当选州长，因此我公开地没能得到一份我非常、非常想要且努力争取的工作。

sentences.en: She lost by less than 55,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 她以不到5.5万票的差距落败。

sentences.en: This is where things get a little complicated.
sentences.zh: 事情在这里变得有点复杂了。

sentences.en: Stay with me.
sentences.zh: 听我说。

sentences.en: In Georgia, the closely watched race for governor has been plagued by allegations of voter suppression and racism.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚州，这场备受关注的州长竞选一直受到选民压制和种族主义指控的困扰。

sentences.en: Abrams was beaten by then-Secretary of State Brian Kemp, who ran as a candidate while simultaneously in charge of the voting process.
sentences.zh: 艾布拉姆斯输给了时任州务卿布莱恩·坎普，他在负责投票程序的同时，又作为候选人参选。

sentences.en: From 2010 to 2018, Kemp oversaw the purging of about 1.4 million recently inactive voters from the rolls.
sentences.zh: 从2010年到2018年，坎普监督了从选民名册中剔除约140万名近期不活跃选民的工作。

sentences.en: It's an action Republican state officials defended as maintaining clean rolls and guarding against voter fraud.
sentences.zh: 共和党州官员为这一行动辩护，称这是为了保持名册清洁并防止选民欺诈。

sentences.en: In 2017, Georgia's state legislature passed an exact match law.
sentences.zh: 2017年，佐治亚州议会通过了一项“精确匹配”法律。

sentences.en: This required the names of voters on registration records to perfectly match their names on approved forms of identification.
sentences.zh: 这要求选民登记记录上的名字必须与他们批准的身份证件上的名字完全一致。

sentences.en: Kemp's office placed 53,000 voter registrations on hold.
sentences.zh: 坎普的办公室搁置了5.3万份选民登记。

sentences.en: The majority were for Black voters, though they could still vote with additional identification.
sentences.zh: 其中大多数是黑人选民，尽管他们仍然可以通过额外的身份证明进行投票。

sentences.en: Several civil rights groups sued the state, and it was amid this legal battle that Kemp ran for governor and won.
sentences.zh: 几个民权组织起诉了该州，正是在这场法律斗争中，坎普竞选州长并获胜。

sentences.en: After the vote, Abrams refused to concede.
sentences.zh: 投票结束后，艾布拉姆斯拒绝承认败选。

sentences.en: I think that Stacey Abrams' election is being stolen from her.
sentences.zh: 我认为斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯的选举结果是被窃取的。

sentences.en: If she'd had a fair election, she already would have won.
sentences.zh: 如果这是一场公平的选举，她早就赢了。

sentences.en: If Stacey Abrams doesn't win in Georgia, they stole it.
sentences.zh: 如果斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯在佐治亚州没赢，那就是他们偷走了选举。

sentences.en: It's clear.
sentences.zh: 很清楚。

sentences.en: It's clear.
sentences.zh: 很清楚。

sentences.en: Democrats claim Republicans cheated, and Republicans...
sentences.zh: 民主党人声称共和党人作弊，而共和党人……

sentences.en: She got a historic number of votes.
sentences.zh: 她获得了历史性的选票数。

sentences.en: I mean, where are the votes that were suppressed?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那些被压制的选票在哪里？

sentences.en: ...claimed there was no evidence of voter suppression.
sentences.zh: ……声称没有选民压制的证据。

sentences.en: Questioning the integrity of the race, I think, is extremely damaging to the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为质疑竞选的公正性对国家极其有害。

sentences.en: She failed.
sentences.zh: 她失败了。

sentences.en: She's got to explain to her donors and keep Democrats agitated.
sentences.zh: 她得向她的捐赠者解释，并让民主党人保持激动。

sentences.en: There's another race coming up in two years.
sentences.zh: 两年后还有另一场竞选。

sentences.en: Ten days after the election...
sentences.zh: 选举十天后……

sentences.en: This is not a speech of concession, because concession means to acknowledge an action is right, true, or proper.
sentences.zh: 这不是一篇承认败选的演讲，因为承认败选意味着承认一个行为是正确、真实或恰当的。

sentences.en: As a woman of conscience and faith, I cannot concede that.
sentences.zh: 作为一名有良知和信仰的女性，我无法承认这一点。

sentences.en: But my assessment is the law currently allows no further viable remedy.
sentences.zh: 但我的评估是，法律目前不允许任何进一步可行的补救措施。

sentences.en: Abrams finally, formally, ended her candidacy.
sentences.zh: 艾布拉姆斯最终正式结束了她的竞选。

sentences.en: Now, all of this may feel familiar,
sentences.zh: 现在，所有这些可能让人感觉很熟悉，

sentences.en: and many people and media groups in the past two months have compared her behavior to that of President Trump's in the wake of his own election laws.
sentences.zh: 过去两个月里，许多人和媒体团体将她的行为与特朗普总统在选举法案后的行为进行了比较。

sentences.en: Here's what she had to say about that.
sentences.zh: 以下是她对此的看法。

sentences.en: When I refused to concede in 2018, what I said very clearly first was that I acknowledged the legal sufficiency of the election,
sentences.zh: 当我在2018年拒绝承认败选时，我首先非常明确地表示，我承认选举的法律效力，

sentences.en: but I challenged the legitimacy of a system that would silence voters.
sentences.zh: 但我挑战的是一个会压制选民的系统的合法性。

sentences.en: By contrast, Donald Trump and his adjutants have falsely pushed a narrative of mythical voter fraud that has been rejected by Democrats, Republicans, by conservatives and liberals,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，唐纳德·特朗普和他的助手们虚假地推行了一种神话般的选民欺诈叙事，这种叙事遭到了民主党人、共和党人、保守派和自由派的拒绝，

sentences.en: by the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 也遭到了最高法院的拒绝。

sentences.en: There is no equivalence between us.
sentences.zh: 我们之间不存在等同性。

sentences.en: Those of us fighting voter suppression are right, and those who are working to undermine our democracy by denying agency to American voters are wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们这些反对选民压制的人是正确的，而那些通过剥夺美国选民的代理权来破坏我们民主的人是错误的。

sentences.en: Agree or disagree,
sentences.zh: 无论同意与否，

sentences.en: what is undeniable is that Stacey Abrams' strategy contributed to getting her much closer than any other Democratic candidate for governor since the party lost state control in 2002.
sentences.zh: 不可否认的是，斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯的策略使她比自2002年该党失去州控制权以来的任何其他民主党州长候选人都更接近胜利。

sentences.en: And, of course, we saw the results in November.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在11月看到了结果。

sentences.en: You are widely credited with pioneering this kind of organizing effort that enabled Biden-Harris to have a successful ticket.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为你是这种组织工作的先驱，这使得拜登-哈里斯能够成功竞选。

sentences.en: What do you say to that sort of praise?
sentences.zh: 你对这种赞誉怎么看？

sentences.en: I mean, you've seen the headlines.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你已经看到了那些头条新闻。

sentences.en: I appreciate the accolades, but I always try to make certain that people understand the other women and men,
sentences.zh: 我很感谢这些赞誉，但我总是试图确保人们了解其他的女性和男性，

sentences.en: the other people of color and white folks who have all been instrumental in building this power and building this opportunity.
sentences.zh: 那些有色人种和白人，他们都在建立这种力量和创造这种机会方面发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: It is disingenuous for anyone to ascribe all of the success to one person, but I understand that I stand as an avatar for what they've seen.
sentences.zh: 任何人将所有成功归功于一个人都是虚伪的，但我理解我作为他们所见事物的化身而存在。

sentences.en: And I think what people are citing without necessarily understanding the backstory is that there were groups that have been toiling in the vineyards for decades.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们在不一定了解背景故事的情况下所引用的是，有许多团体已经在葡萄园里辛勤耕耘了几十年。

sentences.en: She's talking about a story around voter mobilization in the South that goes back much further than 2002,
sentences.zh: 她谈论的是一个关于南方选民动员的故事，其历史远早于2002年，

sentences.en: involving people who have been working alongside her this whole time and also those whose work started well before she was born.
sentences.zh: 涉及那些一直与她并肩工作的人，以及那些在她在出生前就开始工作的人。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So where are we and where are we, like what's the plan for this event that we've just rolled up to?
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在在哪里，我们，就像我们刚刚到达的这个活动的计划是什么？

sentences.en: So we are 24 hours out from the deadline for voter registration.
sentences.zh: 我们距离选民登记截止日期还有24小时。

sentences.en: Organizers will tell you that this is an important day.
sentences.zh: 组织者会告诉你这是一个重要的日子。

sentences.en: And I think what they're looking to do is get the turnout numbers to be just as high as they were in the general election, which is an uphill battle.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们想要做的是让投票率达到与大选时一样高，这是一场艰苦的战斗。

sentences.en: In early December, Robert and I went to Warner Robins, Georgia, about two hours south of Atlanta, to meet with a group called Black Voters Matter.
sentences.zh: 12月初，罗伯特和我去了佐治亚州的华纳罗宾斯，在亚特兰大以南约两小时车程的地方，去见一个叫“黑人选民很重要”的组织。

sentences.en: So they have a small van and then there's another big, it's a big commercial bus and it's emblazoned with the words, we've got the power.
sentences.zh: 他们有一辆小货车，还有另一辆大的，那是一辆大型商业巴士，上面印着“我们拥有力量”的字样。

sentences.en: They've spent the last four months crisscrossing the state with their charter bus, what they call the blackest bus in America.
sentences.zh: 他们过去四个月一直开着他们的包租巴士在全州穿梭，他们称之为“美国最黑的巴士”。

sentences.en: Focusing on organizing black voters in communities that have been traditionally ignored by political campaigns, just as Stacey Abrams has.
sentences.zh: 专注于在传统上被政治竞选忽视的社区中组织黑人选民，就像斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯所做的那样。

sentences.en: The group is officially nonpartisan,
sentences.zh: 该组织正式是非党派的，

sentences.en: but their on-the-ground campaigns largely benefit Democrats and they give money to progressive causes through a separate political action committee.
sentences.zh: 但他们的基层竞选活动在很大程度上使民主党受益，他们通过一个独立的政治行动委员会为进步事业捐款。

sentences.en: I thought that was you, how are you?
sentences.zh: 我以为那是你，你好吗？

sentences.en: I love this talk.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个谈话。

sentences.en: How you doing?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: We run into a woman wearing a Santa hat with a Black Voters Matter button pinned on the side.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了一位戴着圣诞帽的女士，侧面别着一个“黑人选民很重要”的徽章。

sentences.en: She's one of the leaders of the group, LaTosha Brown.
sentences.zh: 她是该组织的领导人之一，拉托莎·布朗。

sentences.en: So, we are here in Warner Robins as we've been doing throughout the election cycle.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们现在在华纳罗宾斯，就像我们在整个选举周期中所做的那样。

sentences.en: We do caravans and so we're getting ready to ride through some neighborhoods and just create a little noise, let people know that Black Voters Matter, we're here, we will be here,
sentences.zh: 我们进行大篷车巡游，所以我们准备穿过一些社区，制造一点动静，让人们知道“黑人选民很重要”，我们在这里，我们将一直在这里，

sentences.en: and there's an important election coming up.
sentences.zh: 而且即将有一场重要的选举。

sentences.en: Am I being something?
sentences.zh: 我是在做什么吗？

sentences.en: Okay, all right.
sentences.zh: 好的，好的。

sentences.en: LaTosha dashes to the bus, and Robert and I, we jump into our own car to follow.
sentences.zh: 拉托莎冲向巴士，罗伯特和我跳进我们自己的车跟在后面。

sentences.en: LaTosha says they're going to make some noise.
sentences.zh: 拉托莎说他们要制造一些动静。

sentences.en: The caravan slowly makes its way past low-slung office buildings and strip malls and turns into a residential area.
sentences.zh: 大篷车缓慢地经过低矮的办公楼和带状商场，转入一个住宅区。

sentences.en: A man and a woman and six kids, they weren't outside but they've come out, and now one of the volunteers is going to hand them a, well, I want to follow him.
sentences.zh: 一个男人、一个女人和六个孩子，他们本来不在外面，但他们出来了，现在其中一名志愿者要递给他们一个，嗯，我想跟着他。

sentences.en: The volunteer hands out flyers with information about the four candidates and a QR code, one of those square barcodes, to help voters get registered.
sentences.zh: 志愿者分发传单，上面有关于四位候选人的信息和一个二维码，那种方形条形码，以帮助选民完成登记。

sentences.en: We need one for mama, Bubba.
sentences.zh: 我们需要给妈妈一张，布巴。

sentences.en: Can I get one more of those for they mama?
sentences.zh: 能再给我妈拿一份吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I'll give you one of these.
sentences.zh: 我给你拿一份这个。

sentences.en: A few houses over.
sentences.zh: 就在隔壁几户人家。

sentences.en: That's how we told y'all, we don't forget about our folks.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这样告诉大家的，我们不会忘记自己的乡亲。

sentences.en: We find LaTosha trying to help a woman get on the Georgia voting website using that QR code.
sentences.zh: 我们发现拉托莎正在帮一位女士用二维码登录佐治亚州的投票网站。

sentences.en: Put your, put your, put your, like your, um, your camera on.
sentences.zh: 把你的，把你的，把你的，就像你的，嗯，把你的摄像头打开。

sentences.en: It's not working.
sentences.zh: 不行，没反应。

sentences.en: Hold on.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: Your phone might, it might pick it up.
sentences.zh: 你的手机可能，它可能识别得到。

sentences.en: Oh no, this is an LG.
sentences.zh: 噢不，这是LG手机。

sentences.en: Hold on, let me find somebody that knows a QR reader, because I don't know how to do it on.
sentences.zh: 等一下，让我找个会用二维码扫描的人，因为我不知道怎么弄。

sentences.en: Every day I phone, I'm a mess.
sentences.zh: 我每天用手机都搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: You know how to do it on a, um, uh, an Android?
sentences.zh: 你知道怎么在，嗯，呃，安卓手机上操作吗？

sentences.en: Is it, um, it's like a app?
sentences.zh: 它是，嗯，它是个应用程序吗？

sentences.en: For roughly 10 minutes, she patiently stands with this woman.
sentences.zh: 大约10分钟的时间里，她耐心地陪着这位女士。

sentences.en: Little two.
sentences.zh: 小二。

sentences.en: Until finally.
sentences.zh: 直到最后。

sentences.en: Okay, there we go.
sentences.zh: 好了，成功了。

sentences.en: It goes through.
sentences.zh: 通过了。

sentences.en: Watching this interaction, it is clear just how different LaTosha's strategy is compared to traditional door knocking or phone banking.
sentences.zh: 看着这次互动，很明显拉托莎的策略与传统的敲门拜票或电话拉票截然不同。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's personal and memorable.
sentences.zh: 这很人性化，也令人难忘。

sentences.en: So that's, I mean, I think it makes a difference that when we take time to really engage people, not just hand somebody something in their hands and act like they don't, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我认为当我们花时间真正与人接触，而不是仅仅把东西塞到别人手里，表现得好像他们不，你知道，

sentences.en: that you're just trying to get something from them, but really take the time.
sentences.zh: 表现得好像你只是想从他们那里得到什么，而是真正花时间去交流，这确实会有所不同。

sentences.en: Hey baby, how you doing?
sentences.zh: 嘿宝贝，你好吗？

sentences.en: Merry Christmas.
sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐。

sentences.en: Are you happy about Christmas?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢圣诞节吗？

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: You like Christmas?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢圣诞节？

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: All right, see you later.
sentences.zh: 好了，回头见。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: She wants everyone to remember that moment.
sentences.zh: 她希望每个人都能记住那一刻。

sentences.en: Remember Black Voters Matter?
sentences.zh: 还记得“黑人选民至关重要”组织吗？

sentences.en: When LaTosha Brown came to their neighborhood and told them how important voting was.
sentences.zh: 当拉托莎·布朗来到他们的社区，告诉他们投票有多重要时。

sentences.en: Just as she remembers her own introduction to the voting process when she was a kid growing up in Mobile, Alabama.
sentences.zh: 正如她记得自己小时候在阿拉巴马州莫比尔市成长时，第一次接触投票过程的情景一样。

sentences.en: You know, my first memory of voting was with my grandmother in Mobile, Nellie Gamble.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我关于投票的最初记忆是和我祖母内莉·甘布尔在莫比尔市一起经历的。

sentences.en: I was her baby.
sentences.zh: 我是她的心肝宝贝。

sentences.en: I mean, she raised me.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是她把我养大的。

sentences.en: I am a grandmama's baby.
sentences.zh: 我是祖母带大的孩子。

sentences.en: How old were you around this time?
sentences.zh: 那时候你多大？

sentences.en: This is probably in the mid-70s.
sentences.zh: 那大概是在70年代中期。

sentences.en: I'm probably around six or seven years old, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我大概六七岁吧。

sentences.en: My earliest memory is that she would put on her dress as if we were going to church.
sentences.zh: 我最早的记忆是她会穿上她的连衣裙，就像我们要去教堂一样。

sentences.en: At our home, my grandmother had this big wardrobe chest and she called it a shiffer robe.
sentences.zh: 在我们家，祖母有一个大衣柜，她管它叫“衣橱”。

sentences.en: And so anytime you went to the shiffer robe to get something, you know, you knew it was special because that's where she kept her like special things.
sentences.zh: 所以每当你去衣橱拿东西时，你知道，你都会觉得那很特别，因为那是她存放贵重物品的地方。

sentences.en: And so I remember she would tell me, go get my good pocketbook.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得她会告诉我，去把我的好手提包拿来。

sentences.en: And so she would, I can see her just as plain right now.
sentences.zh: 所以她会，我现在还能清晰地看到她当时的样子。

sentences.en: I could see her.
sentences.zh: 我能看到她。

sentences.en: And it was something about the way she would put it in the crease of her arm.
sentences.zh: 她把包挎在手臂弯里的样子很特别。

sentences.en: You know, she wouldn't put it on her shoulder.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她不会把它挎在肩上。

sentences.en: She would always put it on the crease of her arm as if she was, you know, in some ways it was like a part of the uniform.
sentences.zh: 她总是把它挎在手臂弯里，就好像，你知道，在某种程度上那就像是制服的一部分。

sentences.en: My grandfather would take us up to the polling site.
sentences.zh: 我祖父会带我们去投票站。

sentences.en: We would go in to vote.
sentences.zh: 我们会进去投票。

sentences.en: And what was exciting is that we would go in this little booth that had curtains, that you would pull the curtains.
sentences.zh: 最令人兴奋的是，我们会走进那个有帘子的小隔间，然后拉上帘子。

sentences.en: And it was just to be grandma and I.
sentences.zh: 那是属于我和祖母的时光。

sentences.en: And we would vote.
sentences.zh: 我们会一起投票。

sentences.en: She would ask me if I wanted to help her.
sentences.zh: 她会问我想不想帮她。

sentences.en: And after she would finish, she would kind of pause, look at me and smile.
sentences.zh: 等她投完票，她会停顿一下，看着我微笑。

sentences.en: And then she would open the curtains.
sentences.zh: 然后她会拉开帘子。

sentences.en: But the way that she walked out of the booth, she would have me by her hand.
sentences.zh: 但她走出隔间的方式，总是牵着我的手。

sentences.en: And her pocketbook on the crease of her arm.
sentences.zh: 手提包挎在手臂弯里。

sentences.en: And she would walk out.
sentences.zh: 然后她会走出来。

sentences.en: And it seemed like she would just walk with her head a little bit higher.
sentences.zh: 看起来她走起路来总是把头抬得更高了一些。

sentences.en: I knew we had just done something special.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们刚刚做了一件特别的事情。

sentences.en: I didn't know exactly what it was.
sentences.zh: 我不知道具体是什么。

sentences.en: But I knew whatever me and grandma had done that day was something that was actually really special.
sentences.zh: 但我知道那天我和祖母所做的一切确实非常特别。

sentences.en: And it made her feel a sense of pride for herself.
sentences.zh: 这让她感到一种自豪感。

sentences.en: And so as I'm older now, I really understand the significance.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我长大了，我真正理解了其中的意义。

sentences.en: Because this is in the mid-70s.
sentences.zh: 因为那是在70年代中期。

sentences.en: My grandmother was born in 1910.
sentences.zh: 我祖母出生于1910年。

sentences.en: So, you know, this is a woman that the vast majority, probably close to 60 years of her life, she was denied the right to vote.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一个在绝大多数时间里，大概近60年的人生中，都被剥夺了投票权的女性。

sentences.en: The notion of voter suppression, of course, has a long history throughout the South.
sentences.zh: 当然，选民压制这个概念在整个美国南部有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: After decades of tactics like poll taxes, long lines, and literacy tests, the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 was supposed to strengthen the enforcement of voting rights.
sentences.zh: 在经历了数十年的投票税、排长队和文化程度测试等手段后，《1964年民权法案》的通过本应加强对投票权的保障。

sentences.en: But in Dallas County, Alabama, for example, African Americans made up half the population but accounted for just 2% of registered voters.
sentences.zh: 但以阿拉巴马州的达拉斯县为例，非裔美国人占人口的一半，但在注册选民中仅占2%。

sentences.en: So this is where civil rights leaders would focus their energy.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是民权领袖们集中精力的地方。

sentences.en: It's also where LaTosha would find herself, a few hours north of Mobile.
sentences.zh: 这也是拉托莎发现自己所在的地方，在莫比尔以北几个小时的路程。

sentences.en: I would spend a lot of time in Selma.
sentences.zh: 我会在塞尔玛待很长时间。

sentences.en: We would go back up.
sentences.zh: 我们会回去。

sentences.en: In Selma, where she had family.
sentences.zh: 在塞尔玛，她有家人在那里。

sentences.en: And my aunt lived there.
sentences.zh: 我姑姑住在那里。

sentences.en: The school system wasn't so good in Mobile at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时莫比尔的学校系统不太好。

sentences.en: So at the age of 11, I permanently moved to Selma with her.
sentences.zh: 所以11岁那年，我搬去塞尔玛和她一起生活，并定居了下来。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that history and the significance of that city?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那段历史以及那座城市的重要性吗？

sentences.en: Well, the first thing I did right was the day I started to fight.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我做的第一件正确的事就是我开始抗争的那一天。

sentences.en: Keep your eyes on the prize and hold on, hold on.
sentences.zh: 紧盯目标，坚持住，坚持住。

sentences.en: You know, Selma is ground zero for me in so many ways.
sentences.zh: 你知道，塞尔玛在很多方面都是我的起点。

sentences.en: It is kind of the center point of my family's journey in this country.
sentences.zh: 它算是我家族在这个国家旅程的中心点。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was something they never really talked about it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是他们从未真正谈论过的事情。

sentences.en: Her family had lived it up close.
sentences.zh: 她的家人曾亲身经历过这一切。

sentences.en: You know, my grandfather is interested in his wallet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我祖父对他的钱包很在意。

sentences.en: He actually carried a receipt for a poll tax.
sentences.zh: 他实际上一直带着一张投票税的收据。

sentences.en: I never knew what it was.
sentences.zh: 我以前从不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: Including the events of Sunday, March 7th, 1965.
sentences.zh: 包括1965年3月7日星期日发生的事件。

sentences.en: The tensions are leaving this place.
sentences.zh: 紧张气氛正在离开这个地方。

sentences.en: And our goal is Montgomery.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是蒙哥马利。

sentences.en: When 600 voting rights advocates set out from a church in Selma to march to the state capitol of Montgomery.
sentences.zh: 当时600名投票权倡导者从塞尔玛的一座教堂出发，前往州首府蒙哥马利游行。

sentences.en: We want some boys in our government.
sentences.zh: 我们需要政府里有我们的人。

sentences.en: My eldest aunt, who was actually one of the women that was, she was beat on the bridge in Selma, Alabama on Bloody Sunday.
sentences.zh: 我最大的姑姑，她实际上就是那些在“血腥星期日”于阿拉巴马州塞尔玛大桥上遭到殴打的女性之一。

sentences.en: You've got two minutes to turn around and go back to your church.
sentences.zh: 你们有两分钟时间掉头回教堂去。

sentences.en: Is that clear to you?
sentences.zh: 听清楚了吗？

sentences.en: That Sunday, that Bloody Sunday, became a catalyst for the passage of the landmark Voting Rights Act of 1965.
sentences.zh: 那个星期日，那个“血腥星期日”，成为了通过具有里程碑意义的《1965年投票权法案》的催化剂。

sentences.en: And so, I knew that there was something that was both prideful and both painful about the process.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道，这个过程既有自豪感，也有痛苦。

sentences.en: So, you know, as I got older and became an organizer, you know, I think now I understand, you know, why my family didn't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当我长大并成为一名组织者时，我想我现在明白了，为什么我的家人不谈论它。

sentences.en: But for LaTosha, it's the foundation upon which it's all built.
sentences.zh: 但对于拉托莎来说，这是这一切赖以建立的基础。

sentences.en: And I also want the world to know about the role of women in the Selma movement.
sentences.zh: 我也想让世界了解女性在塞尔玛运动中的作用。

sentences.en: You know, when we look at the pictures of what happened on Bloody Sunday, when we see how viciously John Lewis and Hosea Williams and Albert Turner were attacked.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们看“血腥星期日”的照片时，当我们看到约翰·刘易斯、何西阿·威廉姆斯和阿尔伯特·特纳遭受了多么残酷的攻击时。

sentences.en: You know, we have those images in our mind, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们脑海里都有那些画面，对吧？

sentences.en: As you're looking at that footage, you're seeing people run back towards the bridge and you see this woman in this beige trench coat that falls in fear of being trampled upon.
sentences.zh: 当你看着那段录像时，你看到人们跑回桥上，你看到那个穿着米色风衣的女人因为害怕被踩踏而摔倒。

sentences.en: That was Miss Amelia Boynton.
sentences.zh: 那就是阿米莉亚·博因顿女士。

sentences.en: She was actually the reason why the Voting Rights Movement started in Selma.
sentences.zh: 她实际上是投票权运动在塞尔玛开始的原因。

sentences.en: It was 10 years earlier where Miss Amelia Boynton actually started organizing.
sentences.zh: 那是10年前，阿米莉亚·博因顿女士实际上就开始组织活动了。

sentences.en: She and her husband had a business and they had organized and she invited Dr. King to come to Selma, right?
sentences.zh: 她和丈夫经营着一家企业，他们组织起来，她邀请了马丁·路德·金博士来到塞尔玛，对吧？

sentences.en: And so it's interesting because I always think about the only, we're seeing this image of this woman being trampled upon
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我总是想到，我们看到的只是这个女人被踩踏的画面，

sentences.en: and not really recognize that she was the true hero, you know, in that day.
sentences.zh: 却并没有真正意识到她才是那天真正的英雄。

sentences.en: And I think it's important to note that because there's a lot of conversation around lifting up the voices of Black women.
sentences.zh: 我认为指出这一点很重要，因为现在有很多关于提升黑人女性声音的讨论。

sentences.en: And I'm so glad that people have discovered us, right?
sentences.zh: 我很高兴人们发现了我们，对吧？

sentences.en: But we've been here all the while.
sentences.zh: 但我们一直都在这里。

sentences.en: We've been here.
sentences.zh: 我们一直都在这里。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is, that Black women have been part of these large movements?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么黑人女性会参与到这些大型运动中？

sentences.en: And why do you think the recognition feels different now?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么现在的认可度感觉不同了？

sentences.en: So I think a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 我想有几个原因。

sentences.en: I think one, I think that Black women uniquely sit at this intersection of sexism and racism, which I call, I think it's the two-headed dragon of oppression
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为黑人女性独特地处于性别歧视和种族歧视的交叉点，我称之为压迫的双头龙，

sentences.en: that has been rooted in America from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这种压迫从一开始就根植于美国。

sentences.en: It's the twin evils.
sentences.zh: 这是孪生恶魔。

sentences.en: And so I think Black women sit uniquely at that intersection of being oppressed because of our gender and also being oppressed because of our race.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为黑人女性独特地处于这种交叉点，既因为性别而受到压迫，也因为种族而受到压迫。

sentences.en: You know, I also believe that oppression can either crush you, you know, or it can transform you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我也相信压迫要么会摧毁你，要么会改变你。

sentences.en: And what I think that Black women have been able to do in this country, you know, it's like a diamond.
sentences.zh: 我认为黑人女性在这个国家所能做到的，就像钻石一样。

sentences.en: All a diamond is, is a piece of coal under extreme pressure.
sentences.zh: 钻石不过是在极端压力下的一块煤炭。

sentences.en: Over time, it becomes a diamond, right?
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它变成了钻石，对吧？

sentences.en: It gets clarity.
sentences.zh: 它变得清澈透明。

sentences.en: It actually, the surface becomes hardened, that it literally, it transforMs.
sentences.zh: 它的表面变得坚硬，它确实发生了蜕变。

sentences.en: And so what I think that has happened in this country is the pain and the trauma
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在这个国家发生的事情是，那些曾经被用来摧毁我们的痛苦和创伤，

sentences.en: and those things that have been used to destroy us, we've used that pressure to transform ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们利用那种压力来改变了自己。

sentences.en: I think that we are Black diamonds.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们是黑钻石。

sentences.en: We're back in Warner Robins with Black Voters Matter.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了华纳罗宾斯，与“黑人选民至关重要”组织在一起。

sentences.en: Their caravan is finishing up the day by serving food to the community and hosting a watch party for a Senate debate that'll start soon.
sentences.zh: 他们的车队正在结束这一天的工作，为社区提供食物，并为即将开始的参议院辩论举办观看派对。

sentences.en: You know, part of culture is a powerful tool.
sentences.zh: 你知道，文化的一部分是一种强大的工具。

sentences.en: I always tell people in the South, culture will eat strategy for breakfast, which is why we take the time, like the music, this is what's natural in our community.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉南方的人们，文化会把战略当早餐吃掉，这就是为什么我们花时间，比如音乐，这是我们社区自然而然的一部分。

sentences.en: We love music.
sentences.zh: 我们热爱音乐。

sentences.en: We play, we love food, particularly in the South.
sentences.zh: 我们演奏，我们热爱美食，特别是在南方。

sentences.en: We use the power of our culture to really be able to make the connection.
sentences.zh: 我们利用文化的力量来真正建立联系。

sentences.en: And so that people are feeling the sense of joy and affirm that Black culture is affirming.
sentences.zh: 这样人们就能感受到一种快乐，并确认黑人文化是具有肯定意义的。

sentences.en: Of course, they also want everyone to vote.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也希望每个人都去投票。

sentences.en: But for LaTosha, it's all one and the same.
sentences.zh: 但对于拉托莎来说，这一切都是一回事。

sentences.en: I want to affirm them that just like that experience with my grandmother, that when I went into the poll to vote with her, I knew that I was doing something special.
sentences.zh: 我想向他们确认，就像我祖母的那次经历一样，当我跟着她走进投票站时，我知道我正在做一件特别的事情。

sentences.en: I felt a part of something special, an experience with her.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己参与了一件特别的事情，那是与她共同的经历。

sentences.en: And I didn't know what voting was, but it was something special about it.
sentences.zh: 我当时不知道投票是什么，但那件事确实很特别。

sentences.en: It was something the way she held my hand, the way she held her head up.
sentences.zh: 她握住我手的方式，她昂起头的方式，都别有一番风味。

sentences.en: You know, and I think we have to create that same sense of pride and a good experience.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为我们必须创造出同样的自豪感和良好的体验。

sentences.en: And when you talk to community members at the event...
sentences.zh: 当你与活动中的社区成员交谈时……

sentences.en: Tell us why you're here tonight, to support Black voters.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你今晚为什么来这里，为了支持黑人选民。

sentences.en: You can hear that messaging.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到那种传达的信息。

sentences.en: And what's important about Black voters?
sentences.zh: 黑人选民的重要性体现在哪里？

sentences.en: We need to vote more.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多地去投票。

sentences.en: Us Black people need to vote more.
sentences.zh: 我们黑人需要更多地去投票。

sentences.en: We need to get this out because all of us Black people need to vote more.
sentences.zh: 我们需要把这个信息传达出去，因为我们所有黑人都需要更多地去投票。

sentences.en: Because a lot of Black people don't vote.
sentences.zh: 因为很多黑人并没有投票。

sentences.en: You know, the younger ones, a lot of people don't vote.
sentences.zh: 你知道，年轻人，很多人都没有投票。

sentences.en: So, like you said, Black vote matters.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像你说的，黑人的选票很重要。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for taking the time to talk.
sentences.zh: 好吧，谢谢你抽出时间接受采访。

sentences.en: Can we ask you a couple questions?
sentences.zh: 我们可以问你几个问题吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: How important are organizations that are grassroots and they're focused on Black voter turnout?
sentences.zh: 那些专注于提高黑人投票率的草根组织有多重要？

sentences.en: They are vital because you get all these, especially like in Atlanta, you know, you've got rich parts of Atlanta that can pump lots of money in,
sentences.zh: 它们至关重要，因为你看看所有这些地方，特别是在亚特兰大，你知道，亚特兰大有富裕的地区，他们可以投入大量的资金，

sentences.en: and sometimes they forget about us more rural counties.
sentences.zh: 但有时他们会忽略我们这些更偏远的县。

sentences.en: And so then you get these people, they come with their fancy bus, and they let these people know, hey, it's not hard to vote.
sentences.zh: 所以，当这些人开着他们的豪华巴士来到这里时，他们会让大家知道，嘿，投票并不难。

sentences.en: They are tackling voter suppression by educating and making voting accessible, and they are so vital, and I'm thankful for everything that they do.
sentences.zh: 他们通过教育和让投票变得便捷来应对选民压制，他们非常重要，我感谢他们所做的一切。

sentences.en: How y'all feel?
sentences.zh: 你们感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: That was the warm-up.
sentences.zh: 那只是热身。

sentences.en: Now, y'all gonna say it like you mean it this time.
sentences.zh: 现在，这次你们要喊出你们的真心实意。

sentences.en: Y'all know we know how to yell in the country.
sentences.zh: 你们知道我们乡下人很会大声喊。

sentences.en: I'm a country girl from Alabama, so we're gonna do this one more game.
sentences.zh: 我是来自阿拉巴马州的乡下姑娘，所以我们要再来一次。

sentences.en: When I say Black voters, you say mad up.
sentences.zh: 我说黑人选民，你们说加油。

sentences.en: Black voters, Black voters, when I say love, you say love.
sentences.zh: 黑人选民，黑人选民，我说爱，你们说爱。

sentences.en: Early voting began in Georgia on December 14th, and the tallies show that more than 3 million ballots have been caSt.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州的提前投票于12月14日开始，计票结果显示已有超过300万张选票投出。

sentences.en: That's already a record.
sentences.zh: 这已经是一个纪录了。

sentences.en: More people have voted in this runoff election than any runoff in the history of Georgia, but overall turnout is still projected to be lower than it was in November.
sentences.zh: 这次决选投票的人数比佐治亚州历史上任何一次决选都要多，但总投票率预计仍将低于11月的大选。

sentences.en: And so far, Black voters represent about 31% of the total.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，黑人选民约占总数的31%。

sentences.en: That's slightly higher than the general election, which might seem to signal an advantage for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这比大选时略高，这可能预示着民主党人拥有优势。

sentences.en: But if the voting patterns of the general election hold, a large number of white voters are expected to vote in person tomorrow, which may benefit Republicans.
sentences.zh: 但如果大选的投票模式持续下去，预计明天会有大量白人选民亲自前往投票，这可能对共和党有利。

sentences.en: If Reverend Warnock and John Ossoff lose on January 5th, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 如果沃诺克牧师和乔恩·奥索夫在1月5日输了，那意味着什么？

sentences.en: Would that be a failure?
sentences.zh: 那算是一种失败吗？

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: I don't know if I think that's a failure.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否认为那是一种失败。

sentences.en: I don't call that, because I don't call wins.
sentences.zh: 我不会那样称呼它，因为我不以输赢论英雄。

sentences.en: You know, for me, an election is not the total determination of a win, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我来说，选举并不是衡量胜负的全部标准，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, I think that what it will mean is, whew, we have a whole lot of work to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这意味着，呼，我们还有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: We've got much more work to do.
sentences.zh: 我们还有更多的工作要做。

sentences.en: I can't even, yes, oh, I just can't take, I can't go down that road right now.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不能，是的，哦，我只是无法承受，我现在无法去想那个方向。

sentences.en: But regardless of who is the winner, we're committed to the longer strategy, which is transforming the South and the state of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 但无论谁是赢家，我们都致力于更长远的战略，即改变南方和佐治亚州。

sentences.en: Would a November win for Biden,
sentences.zh: 如果拜登在11月获胜，

sentences.en: but a Republican win in this runoff in January, would that indicate to you that Donald Trump is a big, a bigger factor in all of this than we think?
sentences.zh: 但共和党在1月的这次决选中获胜，这是否向你表明唐纳德·特朗普在这一切中比我们想象的更重要？

sentences.en: Like, it depends on the numbers.
sentences.zh: 这取决于具体数字。

sentences.en: I certainly, like, I can just say off the top that certainly I think Trump was a factor.
sentences.zh: 我当然可以直说，我认为特朗普肯定是一个因素。

sentences.en: Absolutely was a factor.
sentences.zh: 绝对是一个因素。

sentences.en: I mean, in many ways, I think he's still a factor, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很多方面，我认为他仍然是一个因素，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it's just a matter of, is he going to be a factor in favor of the Republican Party, or does he hurt the Republican Party?
sentences.zh: 这只是一个问题，他是会成为有利于共和党的因素，还是会伤害共和党？

sentences.en: All I can speak to is what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 我只能谈谈我们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: We are doing the work.
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力工作。

sentences.en: The polls say that it's a close race.
sentences.zh: 民调显示这是一场势均力敌的竞争。

sentences.en: We're going to do everything we can to show up and show out.
sentences.zh: 我们将尽我们所能去参与并展现我们的力量。

sentences.en: And I think the numbers will tell the story.
sentences.zh: 我认为数字会说明一切。

sentences.en: On tomorrow's show, a look at the Republican strategy for the Senate runoffs and President Trump's effect on the race.
sentences.zh: 在明天的节目中，我们将审视共和党在参议院决选中的策略以及特朗普总统对选情的影响。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: In a phone call on Saturday,
sentences.zh: 在周六的一次通话中，

sentences.en: President Trump urged Georgia's Secretary of State, Brad Raffensperger, to find him enough votes to overturn his defeat in the state.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统敦促佐治亚州州务卿布拉德·拉芬斯珀格为他找到足够的选票，以推翻他在该州的败局。

sentences.en: The people of Georgia are angry.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州的人民很愤怒。

sentences.en: The people of the country are angry.
sentences.zh: 全国人民都很愤怒。

sentences.en: And there's nothing wrong with saying that, you know, that you've recalculated.
sentences.zh: 说你重新计算过并没有什么错，你知道。

sentences.en: The call, which was recorded, was reported by The Washington Post, which published audio of it on Sunday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 这次通话已被录音，并由《华盛顿邮报》报道，该报于周日下午发布了通话录音。

sentences.en: During the call, Raffensperger repeatedly refused Trump's demands and rebutted his false claims of election fraud.
sentences.zh: 在通话中，拉芬斯珀格多次拒绝了特朗普的要求，并反驳了他关于选举舞弊的虚假指控。

sentences.en: Well, Mr. President, the challenge that you have is the data you have is wrong.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，你面临的挑战是，你掌握的数据是错误的。

sentences.en: Despite the lack of evidence of fraud,
sentences.zh: 尽管缺乏舞弊证据，

sentences.en: 11 Republican senators and senators-elect say they will vote to reject Joe Biden's victory on Wednesday when Congress meets to certify the outcome of the presidential race.
sentences.zh: 11名共和党参议员和当选参议员表示，周三当国会开会认证总统选举结果时，他们将投票反对乔·拜登的胜利。

sentences.en: That session will be overseen by Vice President Mike Pence, who over the weekend expressed support for the effort to invalidate Biden's win.
sentences.zh: 该会议将由副总统迈克·彭斯主持，他在周末表达了对推翻拜登胜选这一努力的支持。

sentences.en: At this point, nearly a quarter of Senate Republicans and more than half of House Republicans will join that effort, which is expected to fail.
sentences.zh: 目前，近四分之一的共和党参议员和超过一半的共和党众议员将加入这一行动，预计该行动将会失败。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗伯特·杰米森和奥斯汀·米切尔制作，埃莉斯·斯皮格尔提供了帮助。

sentences.zh: 由丽莎·托宾剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场残酷、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，和我一起，莎拉·凯尼格，讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.zh: 《地铁》。
